summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic pain, asplenia, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and long-term anticoagulation presented with pleuritic chest pain, fever, chills, and abdominal pain. He reported adherence to Lovenox and recent exposure to a family member with pneumonia. Initial evaluation revealed mild leukocytosis and stable vital signs. A prior CT angiogram from an outside hospital ruled out pulmonary embolism, and a repeat CT of the abdomen and pelvis showed no acute findings, though a stable nonocclusive thrombus near the IVC filter was noted. Empiric antibiotics were started due to concern for infection but were discontinued as symptoms resolved. Hemoptysis was minimal and consistent with chronic anticoagulation. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on his prior medications with instructions to follow up with primary care and hematology for monitoring of a stable lung nodule and kidney cyst.
